title: Home dock Channels, first open in a fresh launch: after its Chromium page attaches, the keyboard is with the Chromium page (its window is key), not with the hidden WebKit stand-in (RED on the feat base: a pre-existing bug)
why: Asked for by the coordinator to cover the FIX case of #29272's review at 976b215 (the pane lookup matched the docked Home's nested Channels page, so its attach skipped its own focus grant). Result, whole host, app active (mini scheduler spec desync-g1w1w4-journeys, 2026-10-31 12:09-12:20Z): the SAME state on all three builds: feat base f2f3083bac80ab71101d03ac (cmux19), #29272 at 976b215 (build 568ad9fbd033e4ba0ac995fb, cmux19) and #29272's head ad21c67 (build ed24b7b111a5fe9b44eaf569, cmux20): Channels in Chromium, its page window visible over the dock and not key, key window ShellWindow, first responder PageWKWebView (the hidden WebKit stand-in), for the whole 10 s. So on the feat base too, Channels in Chromium never gets the keyboard at its first open: a PRE-EXISTING bug, not #29272's, and this journey cannot tell 976b215 from a fixed #29272. It is the red journey of that bug. Code read, not verified: the page's own grant at attach (PageWebView.attachChromium -> focusPage -> CEFTab.setFocused) may wait as a pending focus, and the focus applier's .page case finds no childWindowTab for a nested page (HomeDockView), so it blurs Chromium pages and reclaims the keys for the cmux window. The journey reads the focus state, not typed keys: debug.key's sequence mode has no event timestamp on the capture minis, and the other debug.key modes choose the target window themselves. Needs run.py --whole-host. The frame check (not blank) and the closing daemon check are the harness's required evidence kinds, not the claim.
source: #29272 review finding 1; #29274 review (FIX at c5cba01aa64, comment 6542986147); webviews/src/pages/home-channels/ConversationList.tsx (.lg-search) and Palette.tsx

steps.title: the docked Home shows, with Channels enabled
the keyboard is with the Channels page in Chromium: a Chromium page window is key and the hidden WebKit stand-in is not the first responder; the window is not blank
afterwards (a health check, not the claim) the daemon agrees with the app
